determinism.identity: the ResourceBudget identity is lowercase SHA-256 of the complete canonical serialized bytes, including outcome and non-semantic extensions, and excludes absolute clocks and environmental identity
determinism.ordering: events remain in append order with sequence equal to zero-based array position; exhaustion dimensions and outcome truncation IDs are sorted and unique; vector fields use the exact closed dimension set
determinism.replay: replay starts from zero cumulative and observed usage, processes events once in sequence order, reserves before delegated work, and reconciles each lease once using the dimension-wise conservation equation
determinism.serialization: UTF-8 canonical JSON uses NFC strings, sorted mapping keys, compact separators, ASCII escapes, bounded integers, no floats, and exactly one trailing newline

effects.filesystem: none during construction, validation, replay, serialization, or identity calculation; referenced child ledger bytes are not opened implicitly
effects.mutation: constructed budget, lineage, policy, limit, event, outcome, and extension values are immutable and caller-owned mutable objects are never retained by alias
effects.process: none; this value records independently measured resource observations but does not itself launch, signal, or terminate a process
effects.solver: none; solver calls are exact accounting quantities and validation does not invoke a solver

ensures: ResourceBudget contains one stable budget ID, root or child lineage, one fixed accounting policy, a closed ten-dimension limit vector, one ordered append-only event ledger, one explicit outcome, and namespaced non-semantic extensions.

The cumulative dimensions are exclusive CPU microseconds, solver calls, generated objects, proof bytes, evidence bytes, output bytes, and diagnostic bytes; charge deltas are positive and never spend capacity already consumed or reserved.

Wall time is a monotonic elapsed observation relative to budget start; memory peak and retained bytes observe the inclusive active process tree; nesting records current and peak canonical depth. These observational dimensions are sampled rather than summed across parallel children.

A reserve event atomically allocates all ten dimensions under a unique lease and child budget ID, binds canonical allocation bytes by SHA-256, and fails if current consumption plus all active reservations plus the allocation exceeds any parent limit.

A reconcile event consumes one active lease exactly once and satisfies allocation plus overrun equals child usage plus refund independently for every dimension, with no dimension both refunded and overrun.

Child cumulative usage is added to the parent exactly once; parent wall, process-tree memory peak, and nesting observations must cover the child's elapsed wall time, peak memory, and nested depth without adding parallel observational values together.
Any child overrun requires an exhausted child outcome; a completed child cannot overrun. Reconciliation closes the lease so later spend, refund, or reconciliation under that lease fails closed.

Observed wall-time, memory, or nesting overruns require an immediate exact exhaustion event; attempted requests name precisely the unavailable dimensions and all active children reconcile before parent cancellation or exhaustion.

Cancellation binds its unique ID, source, reason, and latest sampled wall time; exhaustion binds its unique ID, exact unavailable dimensions, positive request vector, and reason; both are terminal ledger events.

Truncation conserves original equals retained plus omitted, omits a positive quantity, binds retained content by SHA-256 unless refusal retains nothing, and the retained quantity was charged to its matching dimension.

Open, completed, cancelled, exhausted, and truncated outcomes bind their permitted ledger state exactly; ordinary completion cannot hide cancellation, exhaustion, observed overrun, truncation, or an active child lease.
Canonical serialization and SHA-256 identity are reproducible without clock origin, process ID, checkout path, backend version, machine identity, or host-dependent measurement units.

epistemics.cancelled: the budget ended because the identified user, parent, or supervisor cancellation was observed at the latest sampled elapsed wall time; no successful completion is implied
epistemics.completed: the ledger closed without cancellation, exhaustion, truncation, observed overrun, or active child lease; this says nothing about mathematical truth
epistemics.exhausted: the exact declared dimensions lacked capacity for the positive request or crossed an observed ceiling; partial work has no success authority
epistemics.invalid: one or more representation, identity, accounting, conservation, observation, terminal-state, canonicalization, or resource invariants fail and no ResourceBudget identity is returned
epistemics.mathematical_truth: not inferred from budget validity, completion, available capacity, producer output, or child outcome
epistemics.open: the ledger is valid but nonterminal and may retain active child leases; it cannot already contain cancellation, exhaustion, or an observed overrun
epistemics.truncated: one or more identified subjects omitted a positive exact quantity under the declared strategy and every truncation is explicitly bound by the outcome
epistemics.valid: all structural and resource-accounting invariants pass after deterministic replay, without attesting that external measurements or child bytes are truthful until independently verified

invariants: The normative schema is docs/contracts/schemas/resource-budget-v1.schema.json=e735dee47394bf50c10ac571dfc8923fd1da851e258b1d9f42e1a66bb9d85e78 and unknown fields fail closed at every object boundary.

The exact limit dimensions are wall_time_us, cpu_time_us, memory_bytes, solver_calls, generated_objects, proof_bytes, evidence_bytes, output_bytes, diagnostic_bytes, and nesting_depth; missing or additional dimensions fail closed.

Policy is fixed to monotonic_elapsed_us wall time, relative_to_start deadlines, exclusive_budget_scope_us CPU, inclusive_active_process_tree_bytes memory, ceil integer rounding, and conservative_all_dimensions reservation.
Root lineage has no parent; child lineage names a distinct parent budget and lease and its allocation_sha256 equals the SHA-256 of the child's complete canonical limit vector.
All identities share one collision-free ledger namespace, event sequence is contiguous from zero, lease and child IDs are never reused, and a closed lease cannot be reconciled or refunded again.

Current consumption plus active allocations never exceeds a limit at charge or reservation; cumulative child values are committed once at reconciliation while wall time, process-tree memory, and nesting remain monotonic parent observations.
For each reconciliation dimension, allocation plus overrun equals consumed plus refund and refund multiplied by overrun is zero; an overrun is explicit and never silently converted to completion.

Memory retained is at most memory peak, nesting current is at most nesting peak, and both peaks are monotonic; a parent observation covers every reconciled child's peak without summing overlapping child observations.

Cancellation and exhaustion require zero active leases and terminate the event ledger; an observed overrun is followed immediately by exhaustion whose sorted dimensions equal the exact unavailable set.

Truncation is permitted only for diagnostic_bytes, evidence_bytes, generated_objects, output_bytes, or proof_bytes; refusal retains zero with no hash and every other strategy retains a positive hashed quantity.

A completed outcome has no cancellation, exhaustion, overrun, truncation, or active lease; cancelled and exhausted outcomes bind exactly one matching terminal event; truncated binds all and only sorted truncation IDs.

Canonical input contains at most 67108864 bytes, 4000000 visited values, 64 nesting levels, 100000 events, 10000 simultaneously active child leases, and 1048576 code points per string; validation is bounded by 30 seconds.

Root extension keys use reverse-DNS namespaces, nested payload mapping keys are at most 128 characters in lowercase snake case, and extensions cannot override core fields, resource state, outcome, identity, or trust.
raises: ResourceBudgetValidationError with kind schema for unknown or missing fields, malformed tagged unions, invalid enums, duplicate JSON keys, invalid scalar types, or noncanonical extension values.

ResourceBudgetValidationError with kind identity, lineage, canonical, accounting, monotonic, lease, conservation, observation, cancellation, exhaustion, truncation, outcome, or budget for the corresponding failed invariant.
MemoryError, KeyboardInterrupt, and SystemExit are never converted into an ordinary valid, open, completed, cancelled, exhausted, or truncated result.
requires: Input is a schema-exact mathhead.resource-budget.v1 object governed by docs/contracts/schemas/resource-budget-v1.schema.json=e735dee47394bf50c10ac571dfc8923fd1da851e258b1d9f42e1a66bb9d85e78.

Limits, quantities, sequence numbers, and accounting vectors are exact nonnegative JSON integers no greater than 9007199254740991; quantities use microseconds, bytes, and exact counts without floating-point conversion.

Event sequence equals canonical array position, every budget, event, lease, child-budget, cancellation, exhaustion, and truncation ID is stable and collision-free within the ledger, and tagged variants contain no unknown fields.

A parent records cumulative charges only for work performed directly in its exclusive budget scope; delegated child cumulative usage is committed exactly once at reconciliation and is never also charged directly by the parent.
Every child ledger is independently schema-, canonical-byte-, and SHA-256-verified before a consumer treats child_budget_sha256, child_usage, child_outcome, or lineage assertions as authoritative.

All strings are Unicode NFC without NUL, JSON values contain no floats, root extensions use reverse-DNS namespaces, nested extension keys use lowercase snake case, and declared hard validation ceilings are satisfied.
